tools.name: simplymeet_get_current_user
tools.description: Return the SimplyMeet.me user that owns the API key (name, email, time zone). Good first call to check the connection. API: GET /panel/api/current-user.

tools.name: simplymeet_list_event_types
tools.description: List the booking event types (meeting types) on the account: name, duration, location, status. Use the ids with simplymeet_get_event_type_availability. API: GET /panel/api/event-type.

tools.name: simplymeet_get_event_type
tools.description: Get one event type by id, including its duration, location type, timezone and questions. API: GET /panel/api/event-type/{id}.

tools.name: simplymeet_get_event_type_availability
tools.description: List the bookable time slots for one event type between two dates. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; pass a time zone name such as Europe/Prague. API: GET /panel/api/event-type/availability/{id}.

tools.name: simplymeet_list_events
tools.description: List booked events, one page at a time, newest first by default. Returns meta (paging) and items (events with invitee, event type and cancellation). API: GET /panel/api/event/.

tools.name: simplymeet_get_event
tools.description: Get one booked event by id: time, event type, invitee, participants, answers and cancellation. API: GET /panel/api/event/{id}.

tools.name: simplymeet_cancel_event
tools.description: Cancel one booked event by id, with an optional reason. Set cancel_following to also cancel the later events of a recurring booking. The event is cancelled on the account; this cannot be undone here. API: PUT /panel/api/event/cancel/{id}.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: simplymeet_get_current_user · Private data: simplymeet_get_current_user · Public sink: simplymeet_get_current_user.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: simplymeet_get_current_user · Private data: simplymeet_get_current_user · Public sink: simplymeet_get_current_user

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
